source: CAMIL GE-V-09 · Page 17 · Ingredients & Utensils for Eating
notes: The page's six example sentences are excluded.
Two three-way collisions carry the page: plate/dish/course are all plato, and
sauce/dressing/gravy are all salsa. Each stays in one unit.
cup/mug are both taza and sit together; glass is beside them for contrast.

area.name: The Table and Tableware
area.description: Poner la mesa y comer: los platos y los vasos, los cubiertos, el mantel y las salsas.

units.name: Plates, cups and glasses
units.topic: What food and drink are served in. 'plate', 'dish' and 'course' are all plato and the unit exists to separate them: a plate is the flat object, a dish is either the deeper object or the food prepared in it, a course is one part of a meal served at a time. 'cup' and 'mug' are both taza — a mug is bigger and has a handle for hot drinks

units.name: Knives, forks and spoons
units.topic: The cutlery and the measures taken with it. A spoonful is the amount a spoon holds

units.name: Setting the table
units.topic: What is laid on a table before anyone sits down, and what a restaurant brings

units.name: Small things on the table
units.topic: The small objects that end up on a table during a meal

units.name: Spices and sauces
units.topic: What food is seasoned with. 'sauce', 'dressing' and 'gravy' are all salsa and the unit should separate them: dressing goes on a salad, gravy is made from meat juices, sauce is the general word
